concerns.message: The plan says the browser tests 'pin the ruin kind for the island through a test-only setting', but `createRuins` takes no kind option. It picks the kind by drawing from the seed (`drawInt(source, 2)` in ruins/state.ts:111), and `generateSequence`/`generateNavigation` are not exported from `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/ruins`. The only way to pin a kind through the exports is to choose the ruins seed: search derived seeds until `createRuins(...).ruins[i].puzzle.kind` matches, or pin a test ruins seed the way `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_FINAL_SECRET` pins the final island.
concerns.consequence: A worker who reads 'pin the kind' as needing a new `kind` option in the pure module stops with `blocked` under the Stop rule ('a pure module change is truly required'). A worker who instead hand-builds a `SequencePuzzle` without the module's uniqueness check can end up with a clue that has several answers, so the browser test's solver fails.

concerns.message: Arrows/WASD are also the sailing keys. In step.ts:54-59, any throttle input whose direction differs from `mooredThrottle` casts a moored ship off, so W/S/Up/Down do it. If the client keeps sending helm input while the navigation panel is open, the ship leaves the dock. `reportPresence` then closes the session, and every answer is refused (`not-at-ruin`/`no-session`). The plan never says the panel takes the keyboard and the helm goes neutral while it's open.
concerns.consequence: Navigation ruins can't be solved in the real client. If Playwright's `keyboard.press` is too short for the server to sample, the navigation browser test may pass anyway while real players get cast off every time.

concerns.message: The ruins module has no disconnect or reconnect operation. docs/ruins.md:47 says the room reports presence 'when a ship moors or casts off' and when `reserveDuel` puts a player in a duel. A disconnect has to be reported as `island: null` while the ship stays moored. A reconnect, the loser's respawn moored at a dock (`returnShip` with a dock) and a settled duel (back to `inDuel: false`) are not moor events at all.
concerns.consequence: If presence is only reported on those events, a reconnected, respawned or post-duel player at a dock gets 'not-at-ruin' or 'in-duel' on R until they cast off and moor again. It would also pass the planned integration tests unless one of them reopens after a reconnect or respawn. Fix: every world tick, derive presence as (connected && docked island ≥ 0 ? island : null, held in a duel), and let the module drop unchanged reports as duplicates. Map dock island -1 to null, since `reportPresence` rejects negative islands as invalid and would leave the old session open.

concerns.message: `open-ruin`/`answer-ruin` arrive through `onMessage`, outside `worldTick`. `worldTick` stops everything once `flow.end !== null`, and ship control is gated on `inPlay()`. The ruins module knows nothing about match phases. `receiveTheftChoice` shows that message handlers rely on the pure module for gating.
concerns.consequence: A player moored at a dock in the lobby or ready countdown could solve before control starts. A player with a session open at the end could solve after the match ends and mint 40 gold into the ledger after the results are frozen, and the HUD gold would disagree with the results table. Gate open and answer on `inPlay()`, and add a row for that branch to the table.

concerns.message: All browser scenarios share one `webServer`, whose test settings are server-wide environment variables (`playwright.config.ts`). `theft-loop` and `full-match` need their islands unlocked (both use Palm Key and Ember Rock, islands 0 and 1). `ruin-solve` and the navigation test need locked islands with pinned kinds. A global 'unlock all ruins' env makes `ruin-solve` impossible on the same server. Every existing integration setup that collects (rubbings, claim, endings, reveals, flowReports, seaDuelSetup, matchFlowSetup) also breaks once sources start locked.
concerns.consequence: Rework and flaky ordering if this is found late, or a 'next match' endpoint whose pending state leaks between specs. Use one island-scoped setting instead, e.g. `unlock=0,1;sequence=2;navigation=3`, parsed in protocol, applied in `createMatchLedger`/`createRuins`, and passed through `matchTuning` in the integration setups.

concerns.message: The branch table requires deleting every branch on a scratch copy and running tests in parallel batches. The Playwright config uses fixed ports (2593/5393, `reuseExistingServer: false`), and several runs share this machine. UI branches whose only failing test is a browser test can't be batched in parallel. Taken together with the server wiring, protocol, DOM panel, two new browser tests, the integration churn and the two carried P2s, this doesn't fit easily in a three-hour worker. `match-online` needed two fix rounds.
concerns.consequence: The worker runs out of time on the table, or marks UI branches as covered only by slow sequential e2e runs. Put the panel's logic in pure web models (clue rendering, answer entry, lockout countdown, HUD ruin state) so that nearly every UI branch fails a vitest unit test, and deletions stay cheap and parallel.

concerns.message: The browser test must 'derive the answer from the displayed clue only'. The sequence clue is English from `tabletText` with 8 relation phrasings ('comes somewhere after', 'does not come last', 'in the middle'…). A solver that parses sentences is brittle, and one that reads a pinned seed's answer defeats the requirement.
concerns.consequence: Either a flaky browser solver, or a reviewer rejecting a test that doesn't read the page. Render each tablet as DOM text plus structured attributes (`data-symbol`, `data-relation`, `data-other`, `data-position`), and each grid cell with its role. The test can then brute-force the 120 permutations or run a BFS from what the page shows.

simpler_alternative: Keep the design, but make three things mechanical instead of event-driven. (1) Derive ruin presence every world tick from the ship's dock, connection and duel hold, and gate the handlers on `inPlay()`. This removes separate hooks for moor, cast-off, disconnect, reconnect, respawn and duel end. (2) Use one island-scoped test setting on the shared server, e.g. `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_RUINS=unlock=0,1;sequence=2;navigation=3`. It covers theft-loop, full-match and both ruin tests on one server without endpoints between tests. Pin the kinds with a seed search over the exported `createRuins`, so no pure module changes. (3) Build the ruin panel as a DOM overlay driven by pure web models. While it's open it takes the keyboard and the helm sends neutral, and the models' unit tests cover the UI branches in the table.
cheap_experiment: A 15-minute script against the current exports, before any worker starts. Call `createRuins({ seed, islands: [0..3].map(i => ({ island: i, sourceIds: [`source-${i}-0`, `source-${i}-1`] })) })` for seeds 0..200. Record each island's kind, the time per call, and the first seed with island 2 = sequence and island 3 = navigation. For every sequence ruin, run the planned test-side solver on `tabletText` output, or on structured hint fields, and confirm it finds exactly the answer. Separately, place a ship at a dock in a dev room, moor it with E, send one frame of W, and confirm it casts off (`dock` becomes `NOT_DOCKED`). The results show whether pinning the kind through the exports is cheap, whether the solver approach is reliable, and whether the panel must neutralize the helm.
